EAGLE-4

One Flexible Drafter for All Batch Sizes and Hardware

Paper (EAGLE-4) · EAGLE-4 draft for Qwen3.8-27B · Documentation


Figure 1(a) of the EAGLE-4 paper: Qwen3.8-27B on the SPEED-Bench qualitative split, 4× NVIDIA B300, one request, temperature 0. The numbers this release measured with EAGLE-4 are in the support matrix.

## EAGLE-4 **Leave speculation on. EAGLE-4 adapts to your hardware, batch and workload.** For high load, serve SGLang on four B300 GPUs with the [high-load recipe](docs/quickstart-sglang.md#high-load), which keeps pace with plain decoding up to 512 concurrent requests. EAGLE-4 (Extrapolation Algorithm for Greater Language-model Efficiency) speeds up LLM inference with speculative decoding. EAGLE-4 draft models are built to run with `eagle-harness`, which decides how far to speculate from measured costs on your setup, so every draft tree fits the batch size, the hardware and the workload. The output stays exactly what the target model would generate on its own: up to 3.4× faster generation on Qwen3.8-27B, with the same answers. [Measured speedups](#measured-speedup) This repository holds `eagle-harness`, the package that brings EAGLE-4 to SGLang, vLLM and TokenSpeed. Install it, point your engine at an EAGLE-4 draft model, and it serves with EAGLE-4. ## Quick start The quick start serves on one GPU and is tested on one NVIDIA B300 with Linux and a CUDA 13 driver. [Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) and its [EAGLE-4 draft](https://huggingface.co/EAGLE-Corp/Qwen3.8-27B-EAGLE4) download on the first start (about 62 GB). The [measured speedups](#measured-speedup) use four B300 GPUs. Add `--tp-size 4` to either serve command to serve on four, and see the [engine guides](#more) for the exact measured commands. raw.description: Ely Office: offline-first desktop apps in Rust and GPUI
raw.readme_excerpt:
# Ely Office

Offline-first desktop apps in Rust and GPUI. Files stay in your folders; no account, no cloud service.

Download from [office.elygpui.com](https://office.elygpui.com) or the [latest release](https://github.com/ELY-Open-Source/ElyOffice/releases/latest): Windows, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (AppImage, deb, rpm, Arch, Nix; Debian 11 and Ubuntu 20.04 or newer).

| App | Does | Engine |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ElyDoc | Word processing (DOCX, ODT) | LibreOfficeKit |
| ElyTable | Spreadsheets (XLSX, ODS, CSV) | LibreOfficeKit |
| ElyShow | Presentations (PPTX, ODP) | LibreOfficeKit, system media |
| ElyPDF | PDF reading and editing, OCR, signatures | MuPDF, Tesseract |
| ElyMail | Mail over IMAP, POP3 and SMTP; follows the system proxy | own IMAP and POP3, mail-send, SQLite |
| ElyTree | Git client | Git |
| ElyMark | Markdown | markdown-rs, RaTeX, mermaid-rs-renderer |
| ElyAgent | Second release | Kigi CLI |

ElyMail signs in to Microsoft with OAuth, and to Gmail and iCloud with an app password.

## Build

```sh
scripts/doctor.sh                 # toolchain versions
scripts/fetch-references.sh       # upstream sources at pinned commits
scripts/build-libreoffice.sh      # patched LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 (about an hour)
scripts/build-mupdf.sh            # patched MuPDF 1.28.5
scripts/build-git.sh && scripts/fetch-git-lfs.sh
scripts/fetch-tessdata.sh
cargo build -p ely-lok --bins -p ely-pdf-engine --bins
cargo run -p ely-doc              # or ely-table, ely-show, ely-pdf, ely-mail, ely-tree, ely-mark
```

ElyMail needs a Microsoft client ID at build time: put `ELY_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID=<id>` in `cred.txt` at the repository root (git ignores it).

The scripts run on macOS, on Windows (LibreOffice under Cygwin, MuPDF with MSBuild) and on Linux inside `packaging/linux/container.sh`, an AlmaLinux 8 image that keeps the binaries on glibc 2.28.

## Release

Pushing a `v*` tag runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Self-hosted runners build macOS (arm64, and Intel under Rosetta), Windows and Linux with `scripts/ci.sh` and upload each app's packages, update manifests and the source archives to the GitHub release. macOS builds are signed and notarized.

## Tests

`cargo test --workspace`; the script tests in `tests/scripts` (the window tests need macOS Accessibility permission; Linux tests run in containers); the benchmarks `tests/perf/bench.py` and `tests/perf/folder-search.rs`.

## Documents

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `PRD.md` | Requirements |
| `agents.md` | Stack, rules and commands; the single source of truth |
| `tasks/TASKS.md` | Progress |
| `docs/decisions.md` | Decision log, by date |
| `docs/help.md` | Help: opening and saving, panels, recovery, offline limits, repositories, mail |
| `docs/compatibility.md` | Compatibility list for the current release |
| `docs/accessibility.md` | Accessibility and language review |
| `docs/perf/` | Benchmark records |
| `docs/licenses.md` | Licences and sources |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Opening a pull request |

## Licence

MIT (`LICENSE`). Third-party components keep their own licences; see `docs/licenses.md`.

raw.description: EL2 hypervisor and toolchain that boots macOS on the ASUS A16 (Snapdragon X2 Elite), with an Adreno Metal/IOGPU stack
raw.readme_excerpt:
# Snapintosh ![Snapintosh — macOS on Snapdragon; ASCII hands reaching toward a red chip](docs/assets/snapintosh-ascii-chip-red.png) Snapintosh boots Apple's macOS 27 (build 26A428) on an ASUS Zenbook A16 laptop with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite (X2E-96-100). It is an EL2 monitor (hypervisor) and the toolchain around it. The monitor runs Apple's stock kernelcache (the J700/T8140 kernel) unmodified by default. It supplies the platform contracts that the kernel expects from Apple silicon: the SPTM and TXM monitor calls, translation of the kernel's 16 KiB page tables, and the Apple devices the kernel looks for. Graphics run on the laptop's own Adreno X2-90 GPU through a driver stack written for this project: - **AdrenoMetal.bundle**: a Metal driver plug-in. - **AdrenoX2**: an IOGPU kernel extension, with **AdrenoDisplay** driving the internal panel. - **air2ir3**: a shader compiler that translates Apple's AIR (Metal's IR) into Mesa's ir3 for the Adreno. There is no software, CPU or paravirtual rendering path. The project also includes an I2C-HID keyboard and touchpad driver (SnapI2CHID), native QCC2072 Wi-Fi work, and NVMe storage through an emulated Apple storage controller. Snapintosh is used together with [q1n1](https://github.com/Snapintosh/q1n1), a UEFI EL2 proxy forked from Asahi Linux's m1n1. q1n1 takes the machine at EL2 after UEFI and serves m1n1's proxy protocol over USB-C to a Mac host, which drives Snapintosh from there. ## Status This is experimental software, written for one laptop model. | Area | State | | --- | --- | | macOS desktop on the A16 | Boots to the desktop with GPU acceleration. Rendering is correct: the pixel checks across the desktop test scenes pass. | | Smoothness | In progress. Interaction is usable but not yet smooth. The target is a steady ~60 Hz first and the panel's 120 Hz later. | | Input | The built-in keyboard and touchpad work, including trackpad gestures, Mission Control and app switching. | | Wi-Fi (QCC2072) | Scanning, a WPA2 connection, DHCP and ping work through a host-proxy harness driven from the Mac. Joining from the macOS Wi-Fi menu does not work yet. | | Storage | macOS is installed on, and boots from, the internal NVMe. | | Other hardware | Audio, cameras, Bluetooth, sleep and external displays are not supported. | [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the details, the known issues and the roadmap. ## Required hardware - An **ASUS Zenbook A16 with the Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-96-100** (UX3607OA). Nothing else is supported. The monitor, device tables, clocks and register addresses are specific to this machine. - A **Mac host** running macOS 27, connected to the A16 over USB-C. q1n1 brings up a USB NCM network link on that cable, and every boot, upload and log capture goes over it. - AC power is strongly recommended. The tools refuse to boot or write the SSD below a battery threshold. ## Architecture in brief ```mermaid flowchart TD UEFI["A16 UEFI firmware"] --> Q1N1 Q1N1["q1n1: UEFI EL2 proxy
(USB-C NCM link to the Mac host)"] --> MON MON["Snapintosh EL2 monitor
SPTM/TXM call emulation, 16K-to-4K shadow page tables,
Apple device models (AIC, ANS2 NVMe, DART, ...), GPU ring and SMMU mediation"] --> XNU XNU["Stock macOS kernel at EL1 + AuxKC
(AdrenoX2 + AdrenoDisplay, SnapI2CHID, ...)"] --> USER USER["macOS userspace
WindowServer, Core Animation, apps
AdrenoMetal.bundle + air2ir3 compiler runtime"] HOST["Mac host: tools/cycle.py, q1n1 proxy client"] -. USB-C NCM .-> Q1N1 ``` ``` A16 UEFI -> q1n1 (EL2 proxy) -> Snapintosh monitor (EL2) -> XNU + AuxKC (EL1) -> userspace + Metal plug-in (EL0) ``` [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains each layer. ## Repository layout | Path | Contents | | --- | --- | | `compat/` | the EL2 monitor: SPTM/TXM contracts, CPU, interrupt, timer and device emulation, the GPU ring and SMMU mediation, the NVMe backend | | `shadow/` | the page-table walker and the 16 Ki

analysis.summary: Экспериментальный гипервизор уровня EL2 и инструментарий для запуска macOS на ноутбуках с процессором Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite. Проект обеспечивает работу нативного графического стека Adreno через кастомные драйверы Metal и IOGPU, эмулируя аппаратные контракты Apple Silicon.
analysis.usefulness: Для энтузиастов и исследователей, заинтересованных в портировании macOS на ARM-архитектуру Qualcomm, а также для разработчиков драйверов GPU, изучающих взаимодействие Metal с не-Apple железом.
analysis.uniqueness: Единственный известный проект, запускающий macOS на Snapdragon X2 Elite с полноценной аппаратной ускоренной графикой Adreno без использования CPU-рендеринга или паравиртуализации, что отличает его от стандартных эмуляторов или портов на Apple Silicon.
pros: Запуск macOS с аппаратным ускорением графики Adreno X2-90
Работа нативных драйверов ввода (клавиатура, тачпад) и Wi-Fi
Собственный компилятор шейдеров air2ir3 для перевода AIR в ir3
cons: Критически высокая уязвимость кода: 7134 находки Bandit и 13 high-рисков в отчёте безопасности
Отсутствие лицензии (NOASSERTION) ограничивает легальное использование и встраивание
